newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bond spreads widen to U.S., Canada.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bond spreads widen to U.S., Canada.

text.p: Australian bonds finished firmer in holiday affected trading on Monday but spreads widened due to their underperformance against U.S. and Canadian bonds.
Opinion polls suggesting that the ruling conservative government in New Zealand could lose power at this weekend's election saw that market weaken, reversing much of last week's narrowing.
The weaker than expected U.S. payrolls report for September released on Friday boosted bond markets around the world.
Australian bonds rallied and remained firm on Monday in thin trade. Sydney was shut on Monday for a public holiday.

However local traders said that while the news was good for Australian bonds, as a bullish market had already fully factored in a 50 point basis cut, the potential for bonds to rally was more limited than offshore.
Three-year bonds were already trading under the official cash rate of 7.00 percent, and 10-year bonds closed at just over 7.50 percent.

In Canada, a further cut after last week's easing was beginning to be expected by the market while the U.S. was starting to reverse expectations of a rate hike, allowing those markets to outperform Australian bonds, traders said.
